title: Sentinel members must preserve singleton identity across copy and serialization
answers: Why must Sentinel implement custom __copy__, __deepcopy__, and __reduce_ex__?
How is UNSET sentinel identity preserved during deepcopy or pickle?
What breaks if Sentinel uses default Enum reduction or copy behavior?
body:
Sentinel enum members used as parameter defaults must maintain singleton identity across shallow copy, deepcopy, and pickle round-trips.
Enforced in src/click/_utils.py:Sentinel by having __copy__ and __deepcopy__ return self, and __reduce_ex__ resolve members via getattr on the enum class.
If skipped, deserialized Parameter, Option, or Command objects fail 'default is UNSET' identity checks and fail deepcopy on Python 3.10.
applies: Sentinel enum implementations and parameter default handling in Click
says: Unset optional flags are mistakenly treated as filled after saving and reloading command configurations.
Cloning command settings causes default values to lose their special unset status.
Reloaded task configurations incorrectly detect default parameters as explicitly supplied by the user.
Ensure unset command options retain their default marker across duplication and background worker serialization.
Duplicated commands confuse missing inputs with provided values because default markers changed identity.
